headline: Unknown: the split and factory surfaces look immutable or ownerless, but OBOL token/governance role authority could not be fully reconstructed on-chain.

findings.text: The pinned ImmutableSplitController returns owner equal to the zero address, while its factory exposes controller/splitMain/create/predict methods and no owner/admin method in the fetched ABI.

The OBOL token contract is verified and exposes AccessControl-style DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, MINTER_ROLE, grantRole, revokeRole, and mint methods, but this run did not successfully read the actual role holders.
The credential NFT contract exposes owner equal to 0x43F641065ea50c57925a1d1668746f65A1Fdea00, plus grantRoles, revokeRoles, and transferOwnership methods; this appears peripheral to validator funds.

The fetched DefiPunkd ABI responses for the ImmutableSplitController and ImmutableSplitControllerFactory report proxy=null; the repo-listed ObolValidatorManagerFactory is Etherscan-verified and its ABI exposes create/read methods but no owner/admin function.
Official governance documentation states a Token House path with 24 hour voting delay and a 5 day timelock, but this run did not obtain the equivalent on-chain governor/timelock constants.

Official governance documentation states proposal threshold 30,000 OBOL voting power, 24 hour voting delay, quorum 0.84% of minted/votable supply, approval threshold 0.01% of minted supply, and a 5 day timelock.

Official governance documentation says Obol Association retains onchain cancel/execution-related authority during progressive decentralization; the exact role holder and scope were not fully read on-chain in this run.

The token mint/grantRole surface is at least economically material if a live minter/admin role exists, and ObolValidatorManager instances include owner/role-gated deposit, withdrawal, consolidation, beneficiary, and recovery functions; however the deployed instance owners and reachable governance path were not fully determined.

rationale.verdict: The assessment is blocked because the immutable split/controller surfaces are readable, but the OBOL token role holders, governor/timelock constants, emergency powers, and complete reachable T1/T2 path were not all reconstructed from on-chain evidence.

evidence.shows: Capability probe succeeded against the protocol website and shows Obol describes itself as distributed-validator infrastructure for Ethereum.

ABI response reports the factory as verified with proxy=null and lists controller, splitMain, createController, predictSplitControllerAddress, and PERCENTAGE_SCALE.

On-chain owner() read returns the zero address for the ImmutableSplitController at block 25144307.
ABI response reports the controller as verified with proxy=null and exposes no upgrade method.

Repo-listed mainnet ObolValidatorManagerFactory is Etherscan source-verified and its ABI exposes constructor system-contract addresses and createObolValidatorManager/read methods, with no owner/admin method visible in the fetched page.
OBOL token surfacer shows DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, MINTER_ROLE, totalSupply, grantRole, revokeRole, and mint methods.
OBOL token ABI response reports the contract as verified with proxy=null and includes AccessControl role-management and mint functions.
Credential NFT surfacer shows owner 0x43F641065ea50c57925a1d1668746f65A1Fdea00 and role/ownership write methods.
Official governance documentation states proposal threshold, voting delay, quorum, approval threshold, 5 day timelock, routing to Obol Association, and Association cancel authority.
Fetched Etherscan page for ObolGovernor shows the contract is source-code verified.
Fetched Etherscan page for TimelockController shows the contract is source-code verified and its ABI includes getMinDelay, schedule, execute, cancel, updateDelay, and role methods.
Official obol-splits repository lists mainnet deployed contract addresses and links audit/release information.
Official bug bounty page lists Obol Splits contracts in scope and describes critical smart-contract impact classes including loss or permanent freezing of funds.

unknowns: C1: Actual holders of DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and MINTER_ROLE on the OBOL token were not read because the role-holder calls with args were not successfully fetched in this run.
C2: Upgradeability of every governance component and every deployed ObolValidatorManager clone was not fully enumerated on-chain.
C3-offchain: Governance delay constants were obtained from official docs, not from live getMinDelay, votingDelay, votingPeriod, or quorum reads.
C4: No Safe-owner endpoint evidence was obtained for any multisig with reachable control; signer thresholds and insider/non-insider classifications remain unresolved.
C5-offchain: Proposal threshold, voting delay, quorum, approval threshold, and timelock delay were not re-read from governor/timelock contracts.
C6: Emergency pause/cancel/guardian powers, if any beyond documented Association cancel authority, were not fully reconstructed from on-chain role reads.
C7: The highest reachable tier on the complete uncontested fast path could not be determined without token role holders, governor/timelock role membership, and deployed manager instance owners.

protocol_metadata.about: Obol provides Distributed Validator Technology for Ethereum staking, letting multiple operators run validator duties through DKG, threshold signing, and fault-tolerant cluster operation. The inspected contracts cover distributed-validator reward and withdrawal recipients, split controllers, the OBOL token, and token-staking surfaces; the fetched evidence does not show Obol itself as a pooled liquid-staking receipt issuer.

headline: Green: stOBOL unstaking and withdrawal-recipient pull claims are directly callable on-chain, with no pause guard found on finalized-claim paths inspected.

findings.text: User-facing exit functions identified in inspected contracts include stOBOL unstake/unstakeOnBehalf, OptimisticWithdrawalRecipient withdraw(address), distributeFundsPull, ObolValidatorManager withdrawPullBalance(address), distributeFunds/distributeFundsPull, and role-gated validator withdrawal request placement via withdraw(bytes[],uint64[],bytes32[][]).
stOBOL's fetched ABI exposes unstake and unstakeOnBehalf without visible owner, role, or pause functions; official docs state users can unstake OBOL at any time directly on-chain.

OptimisticWithdrawalRecipient source shows withdraw(address) as external and ungated by onlyOwner, while ObolValidatorManager source shows withdrawPullBalance(address) as external and ungated; by contrast, validator request placement through ObolValidatorManager withdraw(bytes[],uint64[],bytes32[][]) is onlyOwnerOrRoles(WITHDRAWAL_ROLE).

No pause or paused method was found in fetched stOBOL page searches, and the inspected OWR/OVM claim/pull paths did not show a pause guard; no PAUSE_INFINITELY-style exit freeze was evidenced for finalized claim paths.

No separate emergency-vs-governance pause distinction was evidenced on the inspected finalized claim paths; role-gated OVM functions are for validator deposit/withdrawal/consolidation/recovery operations rather than user pull-claim admission.
Official stOBOL unstaking docs state there are no lockups and multiple staking deposits are handled automatically; no documented on-chain queue was found for OBOL unstaking.

OptimisticWithdrawalRecipient and ObolValidatorManager both include pull-style finalized balance withdrawal paths, and ObolValidatorManager also exposes distributeFundsPull, giving a direct callable path for balances credited to an account.
The official unstaking guide instructs users to use the stOBOL Etherscan Write Contract interface directly and call unstake, confirming an exit path independent of the official frontend.

steelman.red: The red case is that OVM validator withdrawal request placement is role-gated, and a malicious or unavailable role holder could delay validator-level exit initiation for that manager instance.
steelman.orange: The orange case is that some request-placement flows are owner/role-gated and validator exits depend on Ethereum validator lifecycle coordination, even though finalized pull balances appear directly claimable.
steelman.green: The green case is that user-facing stOBOL unstaking and finalized pull-claim paths are directly callable on-chain, no pause guard was found on those paths, and official docs explicitly describe direct anytime unstaking.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because the strongest evidenced exit surfaces are direct on-chain unstake and pull-claim functions with no pause guard found, while the role-gated OVM withdrawal method is a validator request-placement path rather than a finalized user-claim freeze.

evidence.shows: Official guide states Tally staking is deprecated but users can still unstake OBOL at any time directly on-chain, calls the stOBOL contract, and instructs users to call unstake through Etherscan Write Contract; it also states no approval is needed and no lockups apply.

stOBOL Etherscan page is source-verified, exposes Write/Read as Proxy tabs, and ABI includes stake, stakeOnBehalf, unstake, unstakeOnBehalf, rescue, transfer, permit, and delegate methods; fetched searches found no paused or onlyOwner method.

Source shows distributeFunds, distributeFundsPull, recoverFunds with recipient restrictions, and withdraw(address) as an external function that pulls an account balance and sends ETH without an onlyOwner modifier.

Source shows deposit, consolidate, validator withdraw request placement, setBeneficiary, and recoverFunds are owner/role-gated, while distributeFunds, distributeFundsPull, and withdrawPullBalance(address) are external callable paths.
Repo-listed mainnet OptimisticWithdrawalRecipient implementation is Etherscan source-code verified.
Repo-listed ObolValidatorManagerFactory is Etherscan source-code verified and creates ObolValidatorManager contracts.

Official repository lists the mainnet ObolValidatorManagerFactory, OptimisticWithdrawalRecipientFactory, OptimisticWithdrawalRecipient, Lido split factory, Lido split, and immutable split controller deployments.
ImmutableSplitController surfacer shows no withdraw/redeem user-fund exit surface and owner equal to zero address.
Official docs describe Obol as a way to stake ETH on distributed validators and integrate Obol DVs into staking services.
Official bug bounty page covers Obol Splits contracts and fund-freezing impact classes.

unknowns: E1: A complete census of every deployed ObolValidatorManager clone and every product-line-specific user exit surface was not completed.
E2: Access modifiers for all deployed manager clone instances were inferred from source, not from each clone's live verified bytecode.
E3: Role holders for OVM WITHDRAWAL_ROLE, CONSOLIDATION_ROLE, DEPOSIT_ROLE, and RECOVER_FUNDS_ROLE were not read for each deployed clone instance.
E4: If governance or Association-controlled contracts can pause exit-related off-chain services, that off-chain scope was not mapped to a live on-chain pause cap.
E5: Maximum validator-exit queue duration for Ethereum validator exits using Obol tooling was not established from a protocol contract read.
E6: No global adversarial-admin escape hatch was identified beyond direct stOBOL unstaking and pull-style finalized balance withdrawal paths.
E7: Direct callable paths were confirmed for stOBOL and inspected withdrawal-recipient contracts, but not for every manager instance.

headline: Orange: ~0% principal TVS was shown at risk from a single contract dependency, but up to about $1.24B of DV TVL can face performance/yield degradation from operator, relay, API, or module dependencies.

findings.text: External contract calls found in inspected source include ObolLidoSplit wrapping stETH into wstETH and immutable factory-created split distribution through 0xSplits; OVM source references Ethereum deposit, withdrawal, and consolidation system contracts, which are substrate for Ethereum staking rather than protocol-external autonomy dependencies.

Obol's core off-chain dependency is the distributed-validator operator set: docs state DVs are multi-operator clusters using DKG and threshold signing, and the threat model says liveness is lost if fewer than threshold nodes participate while safety is lost if more than two thirds are malicious.
No material bridge or cross-chain messaging dependency was identified for the pinned Ethereum deployment or inspected mainnet split/validator-manager contracts.
The ObolLidoSplit module has one level of nested collateral dependency on Lido stETH/wstETH: the contract receives stETH, wraps it into wstETH, and prevents rescueFunds from rescuing stETH or wstETH.

Live mitigations evidenced for operator risk are architectural rather than on-chain: DKG, no full validator key in one place during normal operation, threshold signing, and multi-operator fault tolerance; no live on-chain fallback was found for a stETH/wstETH failure in the Lido split module.
No appchain, L2 sequencer, or protocol-owned rollup dependency was identified in the fetched evidence; Obol is deployed on Ethereum, whose consensus is substrate for this run.

Relays, beacon nodes, hosted API endpoints, and node operators are liveness/performance dependencies: the threat model says malicious relays can impede communication and malicious beacon nodes can halt or increase slashing risk at Byzantine thresholds, while API docs show bearer-auth hosted endpoints for validator exit-message coordination.

The inspected Lido split stores stETH and wstETH addresses immutably in the constructor, and the repo-listed factories expose create/read methods rather than a setter for swapping these dependencies; no governance-mutable oracle/bridge/module dependency setter was evidenced.

steelman.red: The red case is that validator safety ultimately depends on off-chain operators, beacon nodes, relays, and API/coordination infrastructure, and a threshold-level malicious operator set can create slashing risk.
steelman.orange: The orange case is that these dependencies can materially degrade validator performance, unclaimed yield, or exit coordination, but the inspected contracts and DVT design did not evidence a single external dependency that can directly steal all principal.
steelman.green: The green case is that DVT is specifically designed to mitigate single-operator/key-custody failures through DKG, threshold signing, client diversity, and multi-operator clusters, with Lido-related dependency isolated to the Lido split module.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because the strongest evidenced dependency failures affect liveness, yield, or validator performance across DVs rather than directly permitting contract-level principal theft, while the stETH/wstETH dependency is module-specific and no live on-chain fallback for that module was found.

evidence.shows: Protocol website states Obol DVs secure about $1.24B total value locked and describes distributed validators as securing billions in TVL.
Official docs describe Obol DVT for node operators, staking protocols, and institutions, and describe staking ETH on Obol distributed validators.

Threat model states DKG avoids a full validator key being present in normal operation, sub-threshold nodes losing liveness, more-than-two-thirds malicious nodes losing safety, malicious beacon nodes increasing halt/slashing risk at Byzantine threshold, and relays affecting liveness rather than security.
ObolLidoSplit source stores immutable stETH and wstETH addresses, wraps stETH into wstETH before distribution, and prevents rescueFunds from rescuing stETH or wstETH.

Mainnet ObolLidoSplit surfacer shows stETH address 0xae7ab96520DE3A18E5e111B5EaAb095312D7fE84, wstETH address 0x7f39C581F595B53c5cb19bD0b3f8dA6c935E2Ca0, feeRecipient, feeShare, and rescueFunds/distribute methods.
OVM source shows use of Ethereum deposit, withdrawal, and consolidation system contracts, plus distribution and pull-balance withdrawal paths.

ObolValidatorManagerFactory ABI includes constructor-set depositSystemContract, withdrawalSystemContract, and consolidationSystemContract, plus create/read functions; no external oracle setter is visible in the fetched ABI.
Obol API docs expose bearer-auth endpoints for retrieving and posting validator exit messages and for exit readiness/status, indicating hosted API coordination in the validator exit workflow.
Official repo lists deployed mainnet split and validator-manager contracts and frames Obol Splits as smart contracts for distributed validators.
Bug bounty scope includes Obol Splits contracts and hosted relay infrastructure, corroborating that hosted relay infrastructure is a relevant operational surface.

unknowns: A2: Per-cluster operator count, quorum, operator identity, bonding, and diversification were not enumerated on-chain for all live clusters.
A3: Materiality of any non-Ethereum or cross-chain OBOL/stOBOL deployment was not established from TVS evidence in this run.
A4: The fraction of total Obol TVL using the Lido split module was not measured from contract balances, so the Lido-module dependency share is unknown.
A5: DeFiLlama forkedFrom was not fetched in this run.
A6: No live on-chain fallback was identified for stETH/wstETH malfunction in ObolLidoSplit; mitigation status for every DV-operator failure mode was not reduced to contract reads.
A8: Permissionlessness and redundancy of all relays/API operators used by live clusters were not fully enumerated.
A9: Governance could propose new protocol upgrades according to docs, but no specific live setter that silently swaps an external oracle, bridge, or Lido dependency was identified.

headline: Green: inspected contracts and direct Etherscan/SDK paths are open, while Obol's hosted service applies ToS, KYC, sanctions, and API-auth controls.

findings.text: No contract-level allowlist, KYC, sanctions, onlyWhitelisted, or blocklist gate was found in inspected split factory/controller, Lido split, OWR, OVM factory, or stOBOL entry/exit ABIs; OVM validator operation methods are owner/role-gated but not a public-user KYC admission list.

Hosted Obol API workflows introduce off-chain admission or coordination controls: SDK docs say users must accept Obol terms to create cluster definitions or accept invites, and API exit endpoints require bearer authentication.

Official Terms state Obol may require additional KYC/AML information and may disable the ability to use the Service until documents are accepted; Terms also include OFAC/sanctions representations and a prohibition on unauthorized third-party applications or clients.

Independent access paths exist: stOBOL docs instruct users to call unstake directly on Etherscan, deployed contract pages expose Write Contract tabs, and Obol publishes SDK/API documentation plus open source smart-contract repositories.

No on-chain OFAC, sanctions, or blocklist-checking method was found in the fetched contract ABIs for the inspected core surfaces; compliance restrictions evidenced in this run are Terms/API/client-level restrictions.

Read access is permissionless through DefiPunkd/Etherscan read surfaces; write access is unconditional for factory creation and stOBOL unstake, while OVM validator-operation methods are role-gated by owner/operator roles.

Terms of Service quote: 'Obol may require you to provide additional information and documents at the request of any competent authority or in case of application of any applicable law or regulation, including laws related to anti-money laundering or for counteracting financing of terrorism.' Terms also state the user must not be an OFAC-sanctioned person and must not access the Service through unauthorized third-party applications or clients.

steelman.red: The red case is that the hosted API and Launchpad-style workflows can require terms acceptance, bearer authentication, and KYC/AML document acceptance before using Obol-operated services.
steelman.orange: The orange case is that practical DV cluster coordination may be operationally captured by Obol-hosted API paths even when contracts themselves are callable.
steelman.green: The green case is that no inspected contract-level whitelist/KYC/blocklist gate controls core on-chain entry/exit, and direct Etherscan, SDK, and open-source paths exist outside the hosted UI.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because the grade hinges on contract admission and independent access: the inspected contracts do not evidence a contract-level KYC/allowlist/blocklist, and independent direct-contract paths exist; ToS and API restrictions are reported as hosted-service context.

evidence.shows: Terms of Service state Obol provides a UI to interact with the protocol; Obol may require KYC/AML documents and disable Service access until accepted; users represent they are not OFAC-sanctioned and agree not to access the Service through unauthorized third-party applications or clients.

SDK documentation exists, describes the Obol SDK for creating distributed validators with the Obol API, and states users must accept latest terms to create a cluster definition or accept an invite; it also documents Safe Wallet/RPC integration.
OpenAPI documentation exposes cluster-definition endpoints and operator submission flows, indicating API-mediated hosted coordination surfaces.
DV exit API docs show bearer-auth endpoints for validator exit-message retrieval, posting, and status/readiness checks.
Official guide states users can unstake OBOL at any time directly on-chain by interacting with stOBOL on Etherscan and calling unstake.
stOBOL Etherscan page exposes Write/Read as Proxy tabs and ABI methods for direct staking and unstaking; fetched searches did not find pause or owner gates.
ImmutableSplitControllerFactory surfacer shows createController and predictSplitControllerAddress methods with no listed whitelist/KYC/blocklist gate.
ObolValidatorManagerFactory Etherscan page exposes createObolValidatorManager and read methods; fetched ABI shows no whitelist/KYC/blocklist method.
Official source repository and deployed address list provide a non-frontend path for direct contract discovery and interaction.
Official docs are public and include SDK/API links for integration and direct usage.

unknowns: A1: Every deployed ObolValidatorManager clone and any currently active Launchpad-related contract was not exhaustively grepped for allowlist modifiers.
A2: The exact boundary between hosted API admission, validator-operator coordination, and pure on-chain contract admission was not fully formalized for every user workflow.
A3: Runtime IP geoblocking or wallet-screening behavior on the current official UI was not tested live in this run.
A3b: Third-party frontend or aggregator routing beyond Etherscan/direct-contract and published SDK/API paths was not established.
A4: Absence of contract-level sanctions tooling was based on inspected ABIs/source, not a whole-protocol bytecode census.
A5: Write access for role-gated OVM validator operations depends on instance-specific role assignment that was not enumerated.
A6: Terms PDF was extracted from fetched page text and screenshot, but any dynamically rendered current UI banner text was not captured.

headline: Orange: main contracts are mostly verified and audit-linked, but one pinned Ethereum address has no verified ABI and deployed-to-audited drift was not fully pinned.

findings.text: Pinned ImmutableSplitControllerFactory, ImmutableSplitController, OBOL token, ObolLidoSplit, and credential NFT returned verified ABIs through DefiPunkd; the pinned Ethereum address 0x5754C8665B7e7BF15E83fCdF6d9636684B782b12 returned no verified ABI.
Repo-listed mainnet ObolValidatorManagerFactory, OptimisticWithdrawalRecipientFactory, OptimisticWithdrawalRecipient, and ObolLidoSplitFactory are Etherscan source-code verified exact matches.
stOBOL is Etherscan source-code verified and shown as a proxy/read-as-proxy surface with the implementation address displayed as the same 0x6590... address in the fetched page.

The public obol-splits repository contains contract source folders and a deployed-address list, but this run did not perform an independent compile/bytecode match or pin every deployed contract to a matching commit.

Official audit documentation and repo audit folder list 2023 Obol Splits V1 audit by Zach Obront and 2025 V2/V3 audits by Nethermind; docs say V3 covers the latest Obol Splits including ObolValidatorManager and Pectra-related EIP-7002/EIP-7251 support.

Nethermind and Zach Obront were the fetched auditors for Obol Splits; they are not among the prompt's named broadly recognized Solidity-audit firms, so this audit-recognition signal is not strong enough for green by the prompt's list.

The releases page records audited release commits including v0.4 at commit a53c5ff, v0.3 at 5e26749, v0.2 at 30e5922, and v0.1 at 1524e5a, but deployed-current source drift was not sampled contract-by-contract.

DefiPunkd ABI responses for the immutable split controller/factory and OBOL token report proxy=null; stOBOL's proxy/implementation page is verified; no verified implementation could be assessed for the pinned 0x5754... address because no verified ABI was found.

steelman.red: The red case is that one pinned address returned no verified ABI and the original per-protocol audit_links field was empty.
steelman.orange: The orange case is that most main contracts are verified and audit-linked, but source-to-deployment correspondence and post-audit drift were not fully pinned, and one pinned address is unverified on Ethereum.
steelman.green: The green case is that the official repo, deployed-address list, verified source pages, and 2025/2023 audits cover the main Obol Splits contract family.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because verification and audit coverage are strong for most identified main contracts, but not enough for green given the unverified pinned 0x5754... address, auditors not matching the prompt's recognized-firm list, and unresolved deployed-to-audited drift.

unknowns: V1: Verification status of every deployed ObolValidatorManager clone and every currently used auxiliary contract was not enumerated.
V2: No independent compile, bytecode match, or per-contract source-to-repo correspondence check was performed.
